operations.specification: Service layer: 1) Validate email format and password complexity 2) Check email uniqueness in shopping_mall_customers table 3) Hash password using bcrypt with cost 12 4) Insert new record with email, password_hash, created_at, updated_at, email_verified_at=null 5) Generate JWT access token (15m TTL) and refresh token (7d TTL) 6) Queue email verification notification 7) Return tokens and customer_id in response. Transaction must be atomic.
operations.description:
Register a new customer account using email and password. Upon successful registration, system creates a customer record with email, password_hash, and generated timestamps. The email_verified_at field remains null until email verification is completed. Password is stored using bcrypt hashing algorithm with salt cost 12. If email already exists, system returns 409 Conflict error. This operation creates the foundational account entity for further authentication workflows.

Implementation requires validation of email format, password complexity (minimum 8 characters including uppercase, lowercase, digit, symbol), and uniqueness. The system stores password_hash with no plaintext retention. Generated customer_id is a UUID v4. Upon success, returns JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and refresh token with 7-day expiration. Email verification notification is automatically dispatched with one-time token.

Related to: POST /auth/customer/verify-email, which the user must complete after join to activate account. If user attempts to join with same email again while verification is pending, system returns 409 Conflict with specific error code.

requestBody.description: Credentials required for customer account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and identity details after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service layer: 1) Find customer by email in shopping_mall_customers 2) Verify account is not banned (is_banned=false) 3) Verify account is active (is_active=true) 4) Verify email_verified_at is not null 5) Compare provided password against password_hash using bcrypt.compare() 6) If valid, generate JWT access token with payload {customer_id, email, role="customer", exp=Now+15m} 7) Generate refresh token with TTL=7d and store encrypted in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with refresh_token_hash 8) Return access_token, refresh_token, and customer object. Log authentication success. On failure, log failed attempt counter, increment counter, and lock if exceeds threshold.
operations.description:
Authenticate customer identity using email and password, returning session tokens. System verifies email exists in shopping_mall_customers table and password matches stored bcrypt hash. If account is banned, suspended, or not email-verified, authentication fails with general "Invalid credentials" message. Successful authentication issues JWT access token (15-minute expiration) and refresh token (7-day expiration). Failed attempts increment login failure counter; exceeding 5 attempts in 15 minutes triggers account lockout for 30 minutes.

The login operation relies on email and password_hash fields from shopping_mall_customers table. No additional fields are required for this authentication flow. The password_reset_token field is irrelevant for this operation. Access token includes customer_id, email, and role. Refresh token is stored encrypted in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table with associated access token hash.

Related to: PUT /auth/customer/password and POST /auth/customer/refresh. After successful login, customer gains access to protected routes. If password is changed, all existing tokens are immediately revoked.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for customer authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and customer identity after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Service layer: 1) Find session by refresh_token_hash in shopping_mall_customer_sessions 2) Verify session not revoked and expires_at > now 3) Verify customer_id references valid customer in shopping_mall_customers where is_banned=false 4) Generate new access token (TTL=15m) 5) Generate new refresh token (TTL=7d), hash it, store in shopping_mall_customer_sessions, set previous token to revoked 6) Return new access_token. Return 401 if session invalid, expired, or revoked.
operations.description:
Renew access token using a valid refresh token. Customer presents refresh token obtained during login. System validates that refresh token exists in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, is not expired, and has not been revoked. Upon validation, issues new access token (15-minute expiration) and optionally issues new refresh token (7-day expiration) per security policy. Refresh tokens are rotated per RFC 6749 for enhanced security.

The implementation relies on the existence of shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, which stores refresh_token_hash, customer_id, expires_at, and revoked status. The email and password_hash fields from shopping_mall_customers are not referenced in this operation. The password_reset_token and email_verified_at fields are unrelated to token refresh. Revocation occurs when customer changes password, logs out from all devices, or administrator intervenes.

Related to: POST /auth/customer/login and DELETE /auth/customer/logout. This operation enables persistent sessions without requiring credential re-entry every 15 minutes.

requestBody.description: Refresh token presented by customer to obtain new access token.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access token after refresh token validation.

operations.specification:
1. Receive email and password from request body
2. Validate email format and uniqueness (check in shopping_mall_sellers table)
3. Validate password complexity: min 12 chars, uppercase, lowercase, digit, special char
4. Hash password with bcrypt
5. Create new record in shopping_mall_sellers with status 'pending_verification'
6. Generate email verification token with UUID and expires_at (24 hours from now)
7. Insert verification token into shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table
8. Send verification email with reset link containing token
9. Generate JWT access token and refresh token for session
10. Return access_token, refresh_token, seller_id, email, role, and status in response
operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the platform. This operation creates a new seller record with initial status 'pending_verification'. The system sends a verification email to the provided address, and the account remains inactive until email verification is completed. The seller's password is securely hashed and stored in the password_hash field of the shopping_mall_sellers table. The email field must be unique across all actors. After successful registration, the seller cannot log in until they verify their email address through the confirmation link. This operation aligns with the seller onboarding workflow defined in 03-seller-account.md where registration triggers 'pending_verification' status before administrative approval.

The implementation relies on the shopping_mall_sellers table which contains essential fields for seller registration: email, password_hash, and created_at. The shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table is used to store temporary verification tokens with expiration times to ensure secure email validation. Registration requires only email and password parameters as the rest of the profile details (shop name, description, logo) are completed after verification.

This operation is critical for seller onboarding and must be publicly accessible to allow any business to register. The account cannot be fully activated without email verification, which prevents fake or spam registrations. The system's snapshot principle ensures all registration events are auditable.

The user's email must be validated using the format restrictions specified in the 03-seller-account.md document, and password must meet minimum complexity requirements (min 12 characters, uppercase, lowercase, digit, special character). The password is never stored in plain text.

Related operations: The seller must complete email verification via POST /auth/seller/verify-email before they can proceed to any other operations.

requestBody.description: Credentials for registering a new seller account on the platform.

responseBody.description: Success response with JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account metadata after successful registration and verification. The response includes the seller's ID, email, role, and approval status which will initially be 'pending_verification'.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
1. Receive email and password from request body
2. Look up seller in shopping_mall_sellers by email
3. Verify seller status is 'approved' (reject if 'pending_verification', 'pending_approval', 'rejected', or 'suspended')
4. Compare provided password with stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison
5. If password match: generate JWT access token (expiration: 30m) and refresh token (expiration: 7d)
6. Store refresh token with seller_id and expiration in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table
7. Return access_token, refresh_token, seller_id, email, role, status, shop_name, shop_description, logo_url, created_at, updated_at in response
8. If password mismatch or seller not found: return 401 Unauthorized
operations.description:
Authenticate a seller and establish a session using email and password credentials. This operation validates the seller's credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table and, upon successful authentication, issues a JWT access token and refresh token. The seller's status must be "approved" for login to succeed. Accounts with status "pending_verification", "pending_approval", or "rejected" are denied access.

The implementation uses the password_hash field from the shopping_mall_sellers table to verify the provided password against the stored hash. The session management relies on the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to store the refresh token and track active sessions with expiration times. This ensures secure, stateless authentication while maintaining token revocation capability.

According to 03-seller-account.md, authentication must occur for sellers who have been approved by administrators. The seller's status must be 'approved' before any login attempts are successful. Attempting to login with 'pending_verification', 'pending_approval', or 'rejected' status will return a 403 Forbidden error.

This endpoint implements the authentication flow specified in the requirements and integrates with the password_reset mechanism that allows secure credential recovery. The response includes the seller's complete profile information to support subsequent API calls.

Related operations: This follows email verification (POST /auth/seller/join) and administrative approval (via admin endpoint). The seller must complete both steps before using this endpoint.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for authenticating a registered seller on the platform.

responseBody.description: Success response with JWT access token, refresh token, and detailed seller profile information after successful authentication. The response contains the seller's ID, email, role, approval status, and account metadata used for authorization in subsequent requests.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
1. Receive refresh_token from request body
2. Look up session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions by refresh_token
3. Verify session exists and has not expired
4. Verify associated seller account status is 'approved'
5. Generate new JWT access token (expiration: 30m) and new refresh token (expiration: 7d)
6. Remove old refresh token from shopping_mall_seller_sessions table
7. Insert new refresh token into shopping_mall_seller_sessions with new expiration
8. Return new access_token, new refresh_token, seller_id, email, role, status, shop_name, shop_description, logo_url, created_at, updated_at in response
9. If token invalid, expired, or associated seller is not approved: return 401 Unauthorized
operations.description:
Renew an expired access token by using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication with email and password. This operation validates the refresh token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to ensure it exists, has not expired, and is associated with an approved seller account.

The system uses the refresh token stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to verify authenticity and validity of the token. Upon successful validation, new access and refresh tokens are issued, invalidating the old refresh token for security purposes. This follows the token rotation security pattern.

The refresh token has a 7-day expiration period as specified in the authentication strategy. This allows sellers to maintain authenticated sessions for extended periods without frequent re-login, while still ensuring security through token rotation. All refresh token operations are audited in the session tracking table.

This operation can only be used after successful login (POST /auth/seller/login) following account approval. The seller must have an active, approved account status to use this refresh mechanism.

Related operations: This follows POST /auth/seller/login. The refresh token obtained during login is required as input to this operation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining a new access token without requiring full re-authentication.

responseBody.description: Success response with new JWT access token and refresh token after successful renewal. The previous refresh token is invalidated and replaced with a new one to enhance security through token rotation. The response includes updated token information and seller profile metadata.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Service layer validates JWT and extracts admin context. Ensures admin is authenticated. Creates a new admin account for a user with role 'admin' if user is not already a customer or seller. Validates admin_email (unique), admin_password_hash, and active status. Returns 201 with new admin ID and initial session token.
operations.description:
This operation allows a super administrator to manually create a new administrator account within the system, providing immediate access to administrative controls without relying on an application process.

This is a direct registration pathway (equivalent to 'join') that bypasses standard approval workflows. The system creates an entry in the shopping_mall_admins table with admin_email, admin_password_hash, admin_role='admin', and admin_is_active=true.

Key database schema fields: admin_email, admin_password_hash, admin_role, admin_created_at, admin_updated_at. The admin_password_hash is generated using bcrypt from the password provided in the request body. The admin_email must be globally unique and not conflict with existing customer or seller emails.

This operation is exclusively for super administrators. The system ensures the created admin receives an initial JWT access token and refresh token for login. A session record is created in shopping_mall_admin_sessions.

This operation does not trigger referral notifications or onboarding emails — those are handled explicitly by the user who invokes it.

This operation is available only to super administrators. Access is strictly controlled via the authorizationActor: superAdmin.

requestBody.description: Credentials to create the new admin account including email and password.

responseBody.description: The newly created admin account and authentication tokens.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service layer validates credentials against admin_email and admin_password_hash stored in shopping_mall_admins. If valid and admin_is_active=true, generates JWT access and refresh tokens. Creates entry in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. Returns 200 with tokens and admin profile. Returns 401 for invalid credentials or suspended account.
operations.description:
This operation authenticates an administrator using email and password credentials, granting them a JWT access token and refresh token for subsequent authenticated requests.

Key schema fields referenced: admin_email, admin_password_hash, admin_is_active, admin_is_suspended. The system checks authentication success by comparing the hashed password against the stored value in shopping_mall_admins. If the admin is suspended (admin_is_suspended=true), authentication is denied with 403 status.

This operation is public — no authentication required to access the endpoint. Upon successful login, the system creates an entry in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table with the issued access token, refresh token, and expiration time.

The admin profile returned includes admin_id, admin_email, admin_role, admin_is_active, and admin_created_at. The access token is valid for 15 minutes; the refresh token is valid for 7 days.

This operation is distinct from user/customer login, which uses different tables, schemas, and token rules.

This operation is permanently available for admin authentication. No prerequisites are required. Access is strictly controlled via the authorizationType: "login".

requestBody.description: Login credentials to authenticate the admin.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and profile of the successfully logged-in admin.

operations.name: signIn

operations.specification: Service layer validates refresh token against storage in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. If valid and not expired, generates new access token and refresh token. Extends session lifetime. Updates session record with new token values. Returns 200 with new tokens. Returns 401 if invalid or expired refresh token.
operations.description:
This operation refreshes an administrator’s expired access token using a valid, unexpired refresh token. This prevents admin users from being logged out during extended administrative sessions.

Key schema fields: refresh_token (in Authorization header), admin_session_id, refresh_token_expires_at. The system checks the provided refresh token against the most recent session recording in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. If expired or unverified, the operation returns 401.

Upon success, a new access token (15-minute life) and a new refresh token (7-day life) are generated and returned. The old refresh token is invalidated and removed from the session store. The new refresh token is stored as the active token.

This operation is protected — it requires a valid refresh token to function. It is designed to be called silently when the access token expires, enabling seamless admin experience.

This operation is available only to authenticated admin users holding a valid refresh token. The authorizationType is defined as "refresh". It does not require the JWT access token to be valid — only the refresh token.

No prerequisites are required for this operation. Access is strictly controlled via the authorizationType: "refresh".

requestBody.description: Refresh token to acquire a new access token.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access and refresh tokens for continued admin session.

operations.specification: Creates a new superAdmin account. Validates email uniqueness, hashes password, generates JWT tokens, inserts record into shopping_mall_super_admins table, and creates initial email verification record in shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table. Returns IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized response with access and refresh tokens.
operations.description:
This API operation creates a new super administrator account for the platform. The operation requires a valid email address and password to be provided in the request body. The system checks for email uniqueness across all actor tables (customers, sellers, admins, superAdmins) and rejects registration if the email already exists. Upon successful validation, the password is securely hashed using bcrypt before being stored in the shopping_mall_super_admins table. The system then creates an initial email verification token in the shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table, which will be used to verify the user's email ownership. A JWT access token and refresh token are generated and returned in the IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized response object. This token pair enables the user to authenticate subsequent requests to protected superAdmin endpoints. The creation of the superAdmin account does not automatically grant privileges to manage other users until their account is approved by existing superAdmins, though the account itself is created immediately. This prevents unauthorized privilege escalation while allowing administrators to register in advance of approval workflows.

Security considerations require that this endpoint be publicly accessible to allow initial superAdmin registration during platform onboarding, but subsequent registrations must be restricted to prevent system compromise. Password strength must be enforced using minimum length and complexity rules, and the request body must contain both email and password fields. The operation is specifically designed for superAdmin actor only, and cannot be used to create regular admin or seller accounts.

This operation must be completed before the superAdmin can access any other protected endpoints. The user will need to verify their email using the verification link sent from the email verification process before their account becomes fully active. The system must maintain the initial creation timestamp for audit trail purposes. This endpoint is intended to be used only during system initialization and by authorized platform operators, and should be disabled after initial setup in production environments.

Related operations include POST /auth/superAdmin/login for authentication after registration and POST /auth/superAdmin/refresh for token renewal. The email verification is handled separately through the email verification workflow. The authentication response includes claims that identify the actor as superAdmin, which is used by the authorization middleware to grant elevated permissions.

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new superAdmin account

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing access and refresh tokens for superAdmin

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticates a superAdmin using email and password credentials. Validates credentials against shopping_mall_super_admins table, checks account status (active/banned), generates JWT tokens, and creates a session record in super_admin_sessions table. Returns IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized with refresh token for future renewals.
operations.description:
This API operation authenticates a super administrator by validating provided credentials against the stored credentials in the shopping_mall_super_admins table. The operation accepts email and password in the request body and performs a secure lookup matching the provided email to the corresponding superAdmin record. The system then verifies that the account is active (not banned) and that the password hash matches the provided password using bcrypt comparison. Upon successful authentication, the system generates a short-lived JWT access token and a long-lived refresh token. The refresh token is stored securely in the shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table with metadata including the device type, IP address, and creation timestamp. The access token contains claims identifying the actor as superAdmin and includes its unique user ID and expiration time.

This operation is designed exclusively for superAdmin actors and cannot be used to authenticate regular admins, sellers, or customers. The session record created by this operation enables the system to track active sessions and allows for forced logout across all devices if needed. The response includes both tokens in the IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized format, which is consistent with the join and refresh operations, ensuring compatibility with frontend authentication state management.

The system enforces password policies during account creation, and this endpoint relies on those policies to maintain security. Invalid credentials return a 401 Unauthorized response, while banned or inactive accounts return a 403 Forbidden response. This separation prevents revealing whether an account exists, helping to prevent enumeration attacks. The authentication flow adheres to OAuth 2.0 token-based standards, ensuring scalability and compatibility with common frontend frameworks. Related operations include POST /auth/superAdmin/join for registration and POST /auth/superAdmin/refresh for token renewal.

The access token must be included in the Authorization header of subsequent requests to protected superAdmin endpoints. If the request contains an invalid or expired token, a 401 Unauthorized response will be returned. The low-risk nature of this endpoint allows it to remain publicly accessible, but it should be rate-limited to prevent brute force attacks.

requestBody.description: Authentication credentials to validate superAdmin identity

responseBody.description: Authentication response with access and refresh tokens for superAdmin

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Renews access token for a superAdmin using a valid refresh token stored in shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table. Validates token integrity and existence, regenerates new access token, updates session timestamp, and returns new IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized object without changing the user's authentication state.
operations.description:
This API operation allows a super administrator to refresh their access token without requiring re-authentication with username and password. The operation receives a refresh token (previously issued during login or join operations) in the request body and validates it against the records in the shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table. The system verifies that the refresh token is valid, has not expired, and is associated with an active superAdmin account. Upon successful validation, the system generates a new access token with a fresh expiration timestamp and updates the session's last_used timestamp in the database to extend the session's lifetime.

The refresh token itself remains unchanged and continues to be valid for future requests, maintaining the user's authentication state. This operation is essential for maintaining seamless user experience without requiring users to re-login frequently. The response contains the new access token in the format of IShoppingMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized, but the refresh token is reused, ensuring consistency across the client's authentication state.

This endpoint is only available to superAdmin actors and must be protected behind authentication middleware that verifies the refresh token's validity at the server level. The refresh token must be transmitted securely, typically via HTTP-only cookies or secure headers. This operation helps mitigate the risk of short-lived access tokens being compromised, as the refresh token can be independently revoked if compromised. Related operations include POST /auth/superAdmin/login for initial authentication and POST /auth/superAdmin/join for registration.

requestBody.description: Refresh token to renew access token

responseBody.description: Updated authentication response with new access token

operations.description:
Initiate email verification for a customer account by generating a one-time verification token.

This operation triggers the system to generate a unique email verification token and send a verification email to the customer's registered email address. The token is stored in the shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table and is valid for 24 hours. The operation requires an authenticated customer session and uses the JWT token in the Authorization header to identify the customer.

Security: This endpoint prevents abuse by limiting the rate of email verifications to 3 per hour per customer. If a customer has previously verified their email, this endpoint will return a 409 Conflict error.

Implementation note: This operation does not require request body data since the customer identity is derived from the JWT authentication token. The system will query the shopping_mall_customers table to verify the customer exists and is active before generating the verification token.

Related operations: GET /auth/customers/email/verify/{token} (verify token endpoint) is used to complete the verification process after the email is received.
operations.name: verify
operations.specification: Extract customer ID from JWT token in Authorization header. Verify customer exists in shopping_mall_customers table and email is not already verified. Check rate limit (max 3 attempts per hour). Generate unique verification token using UUID. Insert new record into shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table with token, customer_id, and expiration timestamp. Trigger email service to send verification email with token link. Return 201 Created with confirmation message. For error conditions, return appropriate HTTP status codes: 401 for invalid token, 409 for already verified email, 429 for rate limit exceeded.

responseBody.description: Success response confirming email verification request has been initiated

operations.description:
Verify seller email address using a verification token sent during registration.

This endpoint completes the seller email verification workflow initiated during registration. When a seller signs up, a unique verification token is generated and sent to their email address. This endpoint receives that token and validates it against the shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications database table. Upon successful validation, the seller's account is marked as verified in the system, enabling full access to seller functionalities such as product listing and order management.

Security: The verification token must be a cryptographically secure, single-use token issued only to the registered seller's email address. Token validation ensures that only the person with access to the registered email address can verify the account. Tokens have a limited lifespan (typically expiration within 24-48 hours) to prevent reuse or misuse.

This operation is critical for fraud prevention and ensures only legitimate business entities can become sellers. Only sellers with verified emails can access seller dashboards, manage products, and handle customer orders.

Related operations: POST /auth/register (initiates seller registration and triggers email verification), GET /sellers/me (retrieves verified seller profile).
operations.name: verify
operations.specification: Accept POST request with an email verification token in the request body. Validate the token against the shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table in the database. Check token expiration time - reject tokens older than 48 hours. If token is valid and not expired, update the corresponding seller record in shopping_mall_sellers to set email_verified = true, and mark this verification token as used. If token is invalid, expired, or already used, return appropriate error (400 Bad Request). Clear the verification token record from the database after successful verification to prevent reuse.

requestBody.description: Verification token issued for seller email verification

prerequisites.description: A verification token must be created (or resent) before it can be validated during email verification - this operation generates the token resource.

operations.description: This endpoint validates the email address for an administrator account using a verification token sent to the administrator's email during registration. When an administrator registers, a unique verification token is generated and sent to their email address. The administrator must access this email and initiate a verification request by submitting the token via this endpoint. The system will validate the token against the shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications table, confirming its existence, unexpired status, and association with an admin account. Upon successful validation, the corresponding admin account's email_verified status is updated to true, and the verification token is invalidated to prevent reuse. This process ensures that administrators can only activate their accounts after verifying ownership of the email address, maintaining the platform's high security standards for elevated privileges. The endpoint returns a success response upon successful verification and detailed error messages if the token is invalid, expired, or has already been used.
operations.name: verify
operations.specification: Validate administrator email using the verification token provided in the request body. Lookup the token in shopping_mall_admin_email_verifications table. If token exists and is not expired, update the corresponding admin account's email_verified flag to true, invalidate the token, and return success status. If token is invalid or expired, return validation error. Use database transaction to ensure atomicity.

requestBody.description: Verification token for administrator email validation.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful email verification for the administrator account.

operations.description:
Initiate email verification for a super administrator account.

This operation generates and sends a unique one-time verification token to the super administrator's registered email address. The token is stored in the shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table and is valid for a limited period (24 hours). This operation is triggered when a super administrator account is created, or when a super administrator changes their email address.

The system ensures that only authenticated super administrators can invoke this endpoint. The operation extracts the email address from the authenticated JWT token and creates a corresponding verification record in the shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table. The system then dispatches an email to the super administrator with a unique verification link containing the token.

Upon clicking the verification link, the user is redirected to a confirmation page where the token is validated against the database. If valid, the super administrator's email status is updated to "verified", and the verification record is marked as consumed. This implementation follows the system snapshot principle, where all verification attempts are logged immutably for security audit purposes.

This operation does not create or modify super administrator records - it only triggers the email verification process. The recipient email is automatically derived from the authenticated super admin session. If the super administrator has not yet registered an email address, this operation will return a 400 error.

Related operations: This endpoint is complementary to GET /auth/superAdmins/email/verify/{token} which validates the token. The schema for shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications stores the token, associated super_admin_id, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Generate a cryptographically secure random token (64 characters). Insert a new record into shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table with the generated token, the super_admin_id from the authenticated session, current timestamp, and expiration timestamp (24 hours from now). Send an email to the super administrator's email address with a verification link containing the token. Return { message: "Verification email sent successfully", token: "..." } in the response body.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful email verification initiation.

operations.description:
Resend email verification token to the authenticated customer.

This operation allows a customer who has not yet verified their email address to request that a new verification token be sent to their registered email address. This is a critical capability for users who may have missed, deleted, or not received their original verification email, ensuring no legitimate customer is locked out of their account during onboarding.

The system checks that the customer account exists, the email address has not already been verified, and that the customer has not requested a new token within the last 15 minutes to prevent abuse. The operation triggers the generation and sending of a new verification email with a fresh token valid for 24 hours. The new token is securely stored in the database alongside a timestamp for audit trail purposes.

Security is maintained by never revealing whether an email address is valid or not—users attempting to resend to unregistered emails receive the same response as if the request succeeded. Rate limiting protects the system from email bombing attacks while providing a reasonable user experience.

This operation does not return sensitive data and only confirms success, protecting against enumeration attacks. No user-specific information—including the email address—is returned in the response, maintaining privacy and security standards. The underlying shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table captures all issuance events to support customer support and fraud investigation scenarios without exposing them directly to clients.

Customer-specific actions like this are handled after authentication via JWT, ensuring only the rightful account holder can trigger this action. This operation is not available to sellers or administrators. After successful token resending, the customer may immediately receive the email depending on their email service provider's delivery latency.

Related operations: POST /auth/register (initial registration), GET /auth/verify (email verification endpoint)
operations.name: resend
operations.specification: Retrieve the authenticated customer from the JWT token. Validate that the customer's email is not already verified in the shopping_mall_customers table. Check the shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table for the most recent token issued to this customer. If a token was issued in the last 15 minutes, return a rate limit error. Otherwise, generate a new cryptographic UUID token and insert a new record into shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications with expires_at set to 24 hours from now, is_verified set to false, and the generated token. Queue a background email job to send the verification email to the customer's registered email address. Return a 200 OK response with a JSON body containing { "message": "Email verification token resent successfully" }.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful token resend. No sensitive data is returned to prevent account enumeration.

operations.specification: Verify seller identity from JWT token. Check that seller exists with status 'pending_verification' or 'pending_approval'. Confirm email verification token exists and is expired or not yet used. Generate new verification token with 24-hour expiration. Update database record with new token and timestamp. Send new verification email containing the token. Return 204 No Content on success. Return 400 if seller status is not pending, 401 if token is invalid, 403 if seller has been approved/rejected/suspended, and 429 if rate limited.
operations.description:
Resend the verification email to a seller who hasn't completed the registration email verification process.

This operation allows sellers who have registered but haven't verified their email address to request a new verification email if they didn't receive the original or if the previous token has expired. The system validates the seller's authenticated identity through their JWT token, then checks that their account status is either 'pending_verification' or 'pending_approval'. When validated, the system generates a new cryptographically secure verification token with a 24-hour expiration period, updates the database record, and sends a new verification email with the new token.

Security: This operation requires a valid seller authentication token. Sellers who have already been approved, rejected, or suspended cannot trigger this operation. Rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse of the resend functionality. Email verification tokens are single-use and have a 24-hour expiration window. The email contains a secure link that validates the token and updates the seller account status to 'pending_approval'.

Related operations: POST /auth/register (initial registration), POST /auth/login (account authentication), PATCH /sellers/approve (administrator approval of seller registration).
operations.name: resend

operations.specification: Verify the authenticated admin user exists and is in pending verification state (has admin_email_verification record). Generate new email verification token with expiration. Send verification email using mail service with derived admin email from authentication context. If any step fails, return appropriate error status (401, 403, or 500). If successful, return 204 No Content. No database update needed for the verification record - new token overwrites the previous.
operations.description:
Resend email verification for the authenticated administrator account.

This operation triggers the system to resend the email verification message to the authenticated administrator's registered email address. It is designed for cases where the admin has not yet completed email verification during account creation or when the verification email was not received.

The system will automatically identify the administrator from the JWT authentication token in the request header. No additional parameters or request body are needed. The operation will generate a new email verification token with a fresh expiration time and send the verification email to the administrator's registered email address.

Security considerations: Only authenticated administrators can trigger this operation. The system ensures that the administrator's email address is properly registered and that the token generation conforms to security standards. Rate limiting may apply to prevent abuse of the resend functionality.

Related operations: Admin registration (POST /auth/admins/register) to create the initial account, and email verification confirmation (POST /auth/admins/email/verify).

Note: This operation does not modify the administrator's account status in the database. If the administrator has not been approved by a super administrator, they will remain in a pending state regardless of email verification status.

operations.description:
Resend the email verification token to an unverified super administrator account. When a super administrator registers with the system, they are sent an email with a unique verification token. If this email is not received, is lost, or expires before confirmation, this endpoint allows the super administrator to trigger a new verification email to be sent immediately. This operation does not alter the user's account status or modify any data in the system. It only initiates the re-sending of the verification email, which contains a new time-limited token for authentication. This workflow ensures that super administrators retain access to their accounts even if email delivery fails initially, while maintaining strict security controls by requiring the existing authentication token for identity verification.

This operation assumes the authenticated user is a super administrator whose email has not yet been verified. If the email has already been verified, the system will return a 400 error. If the system is configured to prohibit repeated verification requests within a short time window, the system will return a 429 error for rate limiting. The verification process is subject to the same security policies as initial registration, including rate limits to prevent abuse and denial-of-service attacks.

The verification process follows the principle of least privilege: no administrative permissions are elevated, and no account changes occur during this operation. The operation is stateless, with no requisite data in the request body. Only the standard authorization header is required to authenticate the super administrator identity, which the system uses to retrieve their email address from the database and initiate the new verification email delivery.
operations.name: resend
operations.specification: Using the authentication token, retrieve the super administrator's email address from the users table. Query the shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications table to check if an unverified token exists for this email. If an unverified token exists and is still valid (less than 24 hours old), return 429 Too Many Requests. If no unverified token exists, generate a new 64-character random token, store it in shopping_mall_super_admin_email_verifications with status 'pending' and expiration timestamp (24 hours from now), and initialize a background task to send verification email to the super administrator's email address. Return 200 OK with success message. Disconnect from database and complete operation without waiting for email delivery confirmation.

responseBody.description: Confirmation that the verification email is being resent to the super administrator's email address.

operations.description: Terminate the customer's authenticated session by invalidating their JWT token. This operation triggers automatic session termination by the system as part of its security policy, as customer sessions are managed automatically by the authentication service. No data is deleted or modified - the system simply invalidates the active session token associated with the authenticated customer. This operation is initiated by the user as part of their security awareness and is automatically tracked in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions system, where session end timestamps are recorded. Sessions are managed automatically and should not be manually created, updated, or deleted by API operations. This endpoint exists for user-initiated session termination only, and all session lifecycle management (creation, refresh, timeout) is handled internally by the authentication service as required by system-generated data principles.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: When this endpoint is called with a valid Authorization header containing a customer JWT token, the system will mark the corresponding session in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table as terminated by setting the terminated_at timestamp to the current UTC time. The session token remains valid for the remainder of its expiration window but is marked as invalid for reuse. The session is not immediately removed from the database to maintain audit trail compliance, but future attempts to use this token will be rejected. Cache entries for this user's authentication state are cleared. No data from the customer account is modified or deleted.

operations.description:
Terminate the active session for the authenticated seller. This operation invalidates the seller's authentication token and removes their session record from the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to ensure secure logout.

This endpoint is intended for sellers to explicitly terminate their authentication session. When called, the system extracts the seller's identifier from the authentication token in the request header, locates their active session in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table, and marks the session as expired. The invalidated session token is added to a short-lived token blacklist to prevent replay attacks for a brief period.

The operation is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same session token will not cause errors but will have no additional effect after the first successful invalidation. This endpoint does not affect other sessions the seller may have established from different devices or browsers.

Session invalidation is critical to maintain system security and ensures that compromised tokens cannot be used for unauthorized access after the seller explicitly logs out. No sensitive personal data is returned in the response. Subsequent requests from the client using the invalidated token will be rejected with 401 Unauthorized.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Extract seller ID from JWT authentication token.
Locate active seller session in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table.
Update session record to set expired_at timestamp and status to 'invalidated'.
Add JWT token to short-term blacklist cache with TTL of 30 minutes to prevent token replay.
Clean up any orphaned session-related data in memory.
Respond with 204 No Content status code.
Log session termination event for security audit purposes.

operations.description:
Terminates the authenticated administrator's session by invalidating the access token and revoking the associated refresh token. This operation securely severs all authentication links for the administrator's session, preventing any further access using the compromised tokens. This endpoint requires the administrator to be authenticated via a valid JWT in the Authorization header. Upon successful logout, the server adds the presented access token to a revocation list and invalidates any refresh tokens associated with the session. For compliance and security auditing, the system logs a logout event with the administrator's ID and timestamp.

This logout operation is designed for administrative sessions where security and immediate access revocation are critical. Unlike client-side logout methods that may only remove local token storage, this server-side operation ensures complete session termination regardless of client state. All subsequent authentication attempts with the invalidated tokens will be rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

The operation is idempotent - multiple logout requests with the same token will all succeed without side effects. If the presented token is already invalid or expired, the operation still returns 204 No Content to prevent token enumeration attacks. The server-side revocation system maintains the token in a revocation list for the duration of its original expiration period to handle potential token replay attempts.

This endpoint supports comprehensive security enforcement for privileged administrative access and is a mandatory component of the platform's security architecture to prevent unauthorized administrative actions after session termination.
operations.name: logOut
operations.specification:
Extract authorization header with JWT access token. Validate token signature and expiration. If valid, add token to memory-resident revoked tokens list with expiration matching the token's original exp claim. Retrieve the refresh token's userId from the JWT payload. Invalidate the corresponding refresh token in the database. Clear any cached authentication context for this user. Log logout event with adminId, timestamp, and IP address. Return 204 No Content status code.

For implementation: Use Redis for revocation list to achieve O(1) lookup performance. Set key format: "revoked_token:{tokenId}" with TTL equal to original JWT expiration time. Use database transaction to invalidate refresh token in sessions table. Implement rate limiting to prevent flood attacks on this endpoint.

No fallback handling is needed - token revocation is atomic. If database or Redis fails, return 500 Internal Server Error and log security incident. All revocations must be durable.

Never use clock skew handling for logged-out tokens - if token is presented after logout call, it must be rejected regardless of expiration time.

Process must be completed within 200ms under 100 concurrent logout requests.

operations.description:
Terminate the active authentication session for a super administrator.

This operation revokes the JSON Web Token (JWT) session of an authenticated super administrator, rendering the current session invalid and requiring the user to re-authenticate to regain access. This action immediately invalidates the session token associated with the super admin, ensuring that any subsequent requests with the revoked token are rejected by the authentication middleware.

Security implications: The operation enforces secure session lifecycle management in accordance with enterprise security policies. By terminating the session, the system removes the potential for unauthorized access via stolen or leaked tokens. The logout process does not affect any user data, application state, or database records; it strictly manages authentication state.

Authentication context: All requests to this endpoint are authenticated via an Authorization header containing a valid, active JWT token. The system identifies the super admin session based on the token's payload and correlates it with an active entry in the shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table. Upon logout, the associated session record is marked as expired or removed from active sessions.

Related operations: This operation complements POST /auth/login and POST /auth/register for establishing sessions, and should be used whenever a super admin wishes to voluntarily end their authentication session.
operations.name: logout

Locate the corresponding session entry in the shopping_mall_super_admin_sessions table. Invalidate the session by updating the session's status to 'revoked' or deleting the record. Invalidate the token itself by adding it to a short-lived blacklisted token cache for 5 minutes to prevent replay attacks. Return HTTP 204 No Content with no body to indicate successful session termination. Ensure the operation is protected by the authentication middleware that requires a valid super admin JWT before allowing access.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_customers table to return the display name and phone number of the currently authenticated customer. The customer identity is determined by the JWT authentication token presented in the request header, ensuring that each customer can only access their own profile data.

The service layer retrieves the customer record using the customer_id extracted from the JWT token and returns only the display_name and phone_number fields as specified in the customer account management requirements. This operation supports the customer's ability to view and manage their profile information without exposing sensitive authentication data such as email addresses or password hashes.

Security considerations include proper JWT validation and authorization checks that ensure the authenticated customer can only access their own profile. The operation is protected against unauthorized access attempts through the API's authentication gateway. The response does not include any sensitive personal information beyond what the customer is permitted to view according to business requirements.

Related operations: PUT /customers/me (update customer profile), GET /addresses (list customer addresses), GET /wishlist (get customer wishlist).

Apply caching for 5 minutes with customer-specific cache key. Validate JWT authentication before accessing customer record. Return 401 if token is invalid or expired. Return 403 if customer account is suspended or banned. Return 404 if customer record doesn't exist.

operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed profile information of the authenticated seller. This operation returns the current state of the seller's account as stored in the shopping_mall_sellers database table, including the shop name, description, logo image URL, approval status, and suspension status.

The data returned is sourced directly from the database and reflects the most recent state of the seller's account. The approval_status field indicates whether the seller has been approved ("approved"), is awaiting approval ("pending_approval"), or has been rejected ("rejected"), as defined in the seller registration workflow. The is_suspended field indicates if the seller's account has been temporarily disabled by an administrator, and suspension_reason provides the reason if applicable.

Security: This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated sellers whose identity is verified through a valid JSON Web Token. The service layer extracts the seller_id from the validated token and uses it to fetch the seller’s profile record. No user may access another seller’s profile. Authorization is enforced via the authentication middleware, which ensures the token is signed and issued for a seller account before this operation is invoked.

Related operations: When a seller needs to modify their profile, they should use PUT /sellers/me to update shop_name, shop_description, or logo_image_url. For administrators who need to manage seller account status, use POST /sellers/manage. For review of approval decisions and suspension history, administrators can access seller profile snapshots using the snapshot mechanism defined in the snapshot principle documentation.

Query the shopping_mall_sellers table using the seller_id to retrieve the full record including: shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, approval_status, is_suspended, suspension_reason, created_at, and updated_at fields. Return the profile as a JSON object with these exact field names. JWT validation is performed by the authentication middleware before this endpoint is called, so no additional authentication logic is needed in the service layer. Indexes on seller_id and approval_status are used for query optimization. No caching is applied as profile information can change frequently and must be current.

The operation retrieves data from the shopping_mall_admins table in the database, specifically the fields: admin_id, email, and admin_type. The user relationship is resolved to provide email information.

For security reasons, this endpoint does not return any nested arrays, such as dependent roles or audit histories. Related administrator operations (e.g., managing other admins) must use distinct endpoints and are subject to role-based authorization. This endpoint is strictly read-only and self-referential.

No dependencies on other API operations are required for this endpoint to function. It operates independently based on the authentication context provided by the JWT token.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of shopping mall sections with filtering and sorting capabilities. This operation queries the shopping_mall_sections table to return sections organized in a hierarchical structure based on parent-child relationships. Each section represents a distinct area of the shopping mall, such as 'Electronics', 'Fashion', or 'Food Court'.

Sections can be organized hierarchically with parent-child relationships, allowing for nested categorization (e.g., 'Electronics' > 'Audio' > 'Headphones'). The response includes only essential summary information such as section name, description, and hierarchical level to optimize performance for list displays. The operation supports filtering by section name and description, ordered by creation date or section order index.

Security: This endpoint is publicly accessible to allow customers to browse the mall's layout and section structure. There is no authentication required to view mall sections, though administrators can manage this data via other endpoints.

This operation is used by the frontend to display the mall's navigation structure in sidebars, category menus, and Sitemap pages. It is commonly called when the user opens the website, visits the category navigation page, or searches for products in a specific section.

Related operations: GET /sections/{sectionId} retrieves detailed section information. PATCH /sections allows administrators to create or update sections. DELETE /sections/{sectionId} removes sections.

Key characteristics:
- Returns summary data (not full entity details)
- Supports pagination with configurable limit and offset
- Filters based on name and description text
- Orders by default by creation date (newest first)
- Includes parent-child relationship information
- No request body for simple retrieval - uses query parameters for filtering
- Read-only access - no modification permitted
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sections table with pagination using cursor-based pagination for high performance. Where clause filters by name and description fields using case-insensitive LIKE queries. Join with parent section to include parentName in response for hierarchical context. Order by createdAt DESC (newest first) unless sortBy parameter specifies orderIndex. Limit results to page size specified in request (default 10). Cache results for 5 minutes using request parameters as cache key. For sections with parent, include parent.name and parent.id in response but exclude children array to prevent circular references. Handle case where section has no parent - return null for parent field.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for mall sections.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of mall section summaries with hierarchical context.

operations.description:
Update global configuration settings for the shopping mall platform. This operation allows authorized administrators to modify system-wide configuration parameters that control platform behavior, appearance, and functionality across all user roles and business processes.

The configuration system manages critical global settings including currency code (ISO 4217 standard), timezone (IANA timezone database), locale (language and regional format preferences), payment gateway configurations, tax calculation rules, shipping rate settings, and various platform feature toggles that modify the user experience. Changes to these settings affect all customers, sellers, and administrators uniformly and immediately across the entire platform.

Configuration parameters are stored as a single record in the shopping_mall_configurations database table, ensuring data consistency and atomicity during updates. All configuration values are validated against domain-specific constraints (e.g., currency must be valid ISO 4217, timezone must be valid IANA format) before being applied to prevent invalid states.

Due to the system-critical nature of these configurations, this operation requires elevated administrative privileges. Configuration changes are logged in an audit trail with detailed information about who made the change, when it was made, and what values were changed from and to, for compliance and troubleshooting purposes.

To ensure system stability and performance, successfully updated configurations are cached in memory for five minutes to avoid redundant database reads. The cache is automatically invalidated on subsequent configuration changes or system restarts.

This configuration endpoint follows the principle of centralized system control, ensuring that global platform settings cannot be overridden or modified through individual user actions or distributed system components.

Generate snapshot of configuration state before update. Log update action with actor details and timestamp in audit trail. Return updated configuration object with all fields including metadata and audit information.
operations.description:
Update a system configuration setting by its unique configuration identifier.

This operation allows authorized administrators to modify critical platform settings stored in the shopping_mall_configurations table. Each configuration represents a system parameter that controls functionality such as payment processing thresholds, shipping default values, marketplace fee structures, or display preferences. Examples include minimum_order_value for order fulfillment, max_upload_size for media, or default_currency for international pricing.

The configurationId parameter identifies the specific configuration setting to update, which corresponds to the unique identifier in the shopping_mall_configurations table. The request body provides the new values for the configuration, including the value field and optional metadata such as description or context.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrator privileges. Unauthorized attempts will be rejected. All configuration changes trigger automatic system behavior: audit logs are created to record actor information and timestamps, and a snapshot of the configuration state is preserved as part of the comprehensive snapshot mechanism to ensure compliance and historical traceability.

Business rules enforce validation of configuration values against predefined constraints defined in the database schema. For example, numeric values must remain within acceptable ranges, string values must conform to required formats, and boolean values must be strictly true or false. Invalid configurations will be rejected with appropriate error codes.

Related operations: GET /configurations to retrieve configuration settings, GET /configurations/{configurationId} to view a specific configuration in detail, and GET /configurations/snapshots to review historical configuration changes.

operations.description:
Update an existing product's information including name, description, category ID, and base price. This operation implements the product lifecycle management requirements specified in the system, creating a comprehensive snapshot of the product state before modification to ensure historical accuracy for audit, compliance, and dispute resolution purposes.

When a seller updates a product, the system captures the complete previous state including all product details and image sequences in an immutable product snapshot. This snapshot preserves the product's configuration as it existed at the moment of change, including the product name, description, category assignment, base price, and image order sequence. The snapshot mechanism ensures that all historical states of the product are preserved for future reference, even if the product is later modified again or deleted.

The operation enforces ownership validation, ensuring that only the seller who created the product is permitted to make updates. This prevents unauthorized modification of product details by other sellers or users. Additionally, any updates to the product's category or base price are logged in the snapshot with the timestamp and actor information to maintain complete audit trails. The product's variant information remains unaffected by changes to these top-level fields, maintaining data integrity across the product ecosystem.

The snapshot system ensures complete traceability of product changes, supporting regulatory compliance, customer disputes, and business analytics. For example, if a customer received a product that differed from its specifications at time of purchase, the historical product snapshot can be used to verify compliance. Similarly, administrators can audit product modifications to ensure adherence to platform policies and identify patterns of abuse or error. The system maintains the integrity of the product record by preventing direct alteration of historical states while enabling current data to be updated as needed.

This operation does not modify product variants, images, or inventory levels, which have separate dedicated endpoints. Changes to product variants require the /products/{productId}/variants endpoint, while image modifications use the /products/{productId}/images endpoint. This separation of concerns ensures consistent data integrity while allowing each domain to manage its specific lifecycle requirements.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update product fields (name, description, category, base price) only if user is the product owner.
Validate the product owner matches the authenticated seller ID.
Create a product snapshot capturing:
- Previous name, description, category ID, base price
- Current values after update
- Timestamp of change
- Actor (seller ID)
- Current image sequence with all image identifiers in order
- Variant count (not the variants themselves, as variants are separate entities)
- Do not modify any variant information
- If no fields provided in request, return 400 Bad Request with message 'No fields to update'
- If product not found, return 404 Not Found
- If seller is not owner, return 403 Forbidden with message 'Not authorized to update this product'
- Do not validate product name uniqueness (already handled during creation)
- Only update fields provided in request - do not modify fields omitted from the request
- Return 200 OK with updated product fields upon successful update

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product. Must be a UUID format string that corresponds to the shopping_mall_products table's primary key.

requestBody.description: Update request for product information with optional fields for product name, description, category, and base price.

responseBody.description: Updated product resource after successful modification.

prerequisites.description: Category must exist before a product can reference it during update operations, as categoryId must reference a valid category in the shopping_mall_categories table.

operations.specification: Delete the product record from the shopping_mall_products table using the productId path parameter. Cascade delete all associated records in shopping_mall_product_images and shopping_mall_product_variants tables. Check that the product has no order items with status 'paid', 'shipped', or 'delivered'. If order items exist with these statuses, return 400 with error message. Verify that the requesting user is either the product's seller or has admin privileges. If not, return 403 Forbidden. Log the deletion in the audit trail. Return the deleted product record in the response body including its id, name, sellerId, and createdAt timestamp for audit purposes.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a product from the shopping mall platform. This operation completely deletes the product record from the database and cascades deletion to all associated resources including product images and variants.

This is a hard delete operation — records are permanently removed and cannot be recovered. This behavior is intentional as specified by the business requirements which indicate product deletion should be irreversible. After this operation, the product will no longer appear in search results, product listings, or any customer-facing interfaces.

Security considerations include strict authorization: only the original seller who created the product may perform this operation, unless the requester has administrative privileges. The system performs additional validation to ensure the product does not have any associated order items with status 'paid', 'shipped', or 'delivered' to prevent disruption of existing customer transactions. If such order items exist, the deletion will be blocked with a 400 error. This prevents the accidental deletion of products that are part of active or completed customer orders.

This operation is intended for two primary use cases: when a seller removes an unsold product from their inventory, or when an administrator enforces content moderation policies by removing products that violate platform guidelines. The product's deletion history is preserved in audit logs for compliance and security review.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product. This UUID refers to the product record in the shopping_mall_products table.

responseBody.description: The deleted product record returned as confirmation for audit and record keeping purposes.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be referenced in order items and subsequently deleted.

operations.description:
Upload images for a specific product listing in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows authenticated sellers to upload multiple image files associated with a specific product. Each uploaded image will be stored as a separate record in the shopping_mall_product_images table, with the imageUrl field containing the generated URI reference to the image asset, and imageOrder field determining its display order.

Security: The request must be authenticated as a seller account. The system will validate that the seller has ownership of the product specified by productId. Only product images associated with the seller's products may be uploaded.

Implementation: Images are stored in an object storage system (S3-compatible). The URI for each uploaded image is generated in the service layer after successful upload. The imageOrder field is automatically assigned based on upload sequence, starting from 1 for the first image. The system may compress large images and generate web-friendly variants (WebP/AVIF) for optimized delivery.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/images (list product images), PUT /products/{productId}/images/reorder (reorder product images), DELETE /products/{productId}/images/{imageId} (delete specific image).
operations.name: create
operations.specification: On POST request to /products/{productId}/images, authenticate the user as a seller and verify seller ownership of the product. Extract the productId from the path parameter. Create a new record for each uploaded image in the shopping_mall_product_images table. Generate a unique URI for each image file using the storage system. Assign imageOrder sequentially based on the upload order (1, 2, 3, ...). Store the generated URI in the imageUrl field. Ensure file uploads are properly validated for size and type (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF). Return each successfully uploaded image's details including the generated imageId, imageUrl, and assigned imageOrder in the response body, following the IShoppingMallProductImage schema.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to which images will be uploaded
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Sets of image files to be uploaded as a list of URI strings pointing to uploaded assets. This setup supports multiple image uploads in one request, each represented by its URI reference.

responseBody.description: Array of successfully uploaded product image records, each including generated image identifiers, storage URIs, and display order.

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before images can be uploaded to it, as the productId path parameter references an existing product entity.

operations.description:
Reorder the sequence of product images for a specific product. This operation allows sellers to manually arrange the visual order of images displayed on the product detail page, ensuring the most important or featured images appear first.

Sellers can update the sequence of all images associated with a product in a single atomic operation. The request body must contain every image associated with the product, specifying a new imageOrder value for each. If any image is omitted from the request, it will be treated as having been removed from the ordered set, which will trigger an error. This ensures data integrity and prevents unintended deletion of image order information.

The operation requires the requester to be an authenticated seller with permission to manage the specified product. No other actors are permitted to reorder images.

This operation complements the POST /products/{productId}/images endpoint, which uploads new images, and the DELETE /products/{productId}/images/{imageId} endpoint, which removes images. The reorder operation specifically manages the presentation sequence of existing images.
operations.name: reorder
operations.specification: Query all product images for the given productId. Validate that all images in the request body are from this product. Update the imageOrder field of each image using the supplied values in a database transaction. Ensure that no two images receive the same imageOrder value. Calculate a new sequence from 0 to N-1 for each image. Generate a product snapshot if the image order has changed from the previous state (compare older imageOrder values to new ones). Log the action with the actorId of the authenticated seller. Return the updated list of images in new order with their updated imageOrder values as confirmation.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product whose images are being reordered.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: An array of image objects specifying each image's ID and its new relative display order.

responseBody.description: The list of product images with their updated imageOrder values after successful reordering.

prerequisites.description: Product images must exist before they can be reordered in the gallery sequence

operations.description:
Delete a specific product image associated with a product. This operation permanently removes an image from the product's image gallery. The image is removed from the shopping_mall_product_images table and its URL is no longer accessible.

Security: This operation requires authentication as the seller who owns the product. Unauthorized access attempts by other users or non-sellers will be rejected. The system verifies that the specified product exists and that the authenticated seller is the owner of the product before allowing the delete operation.

Behavior: If the product has multiple images, deletion proceeds successfully. If this is the last image of the product, the system does NOT automatically generate a replacement. The product remains visible in search with no primary image, which may affect customer perception.

Side effects: This operation triggers a product snapshot event, capturing the state of the product's image gallery before the deletion, as required by the 14-snapshot-principle.md documentation.

Implementation: The system performs a direct delete query on shopping_mall_product_images table using product_id and image_id as composite keys. Image file storage deletion is handled asynchronously by a file system cleanup service after successful database deletion.

Related operations: POST /products/{productId}/images (upload), PUT /products/{productId}/images/reorder (reorder), DELETE /products/{productId} (delete entire product).
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_product_images table with product_id and image_id as composite key. Verify user is owner of the product by joining with shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_sellers tables. Perform database deletion if validation passes. Schedule asynchronous file system cleanup for the image file. Create a product snapshot capturing the current state of all images before deletion.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product containing the image to be deleted. This is a UUID value from the shopping_mall_products table.
parameters.name: productId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific image to be deleted from the product. This is a UUID value from the shopping_mall_product_images table.
