operations.specification: Delete the refund request record with the specified ID from the shopping_mall_refund_requests table. This is a hard delete operation that permanently removes the record. Before deletion, validate that the request exists and that the requester has appropriate permissions. If the refund request status is 'approved' or 'processed', return 400 error to prevent deletion of completed requests. Log the deletion event in the audit system with the user ID who performed the deletion.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a refund request from the system. This operation removes the refund request record with the specified ID from the shopping_mall_refund_requests database table. This action cannot be undone and no trace of the record will remain in the database.

The operation requires authentication and authorization to ensure that only the customer who initiated the refund request or an administrator with appropriate permissions can delete it. The refund request ID must be passed as a path parameter in the format of a UUID. Any request attempting to delete a non-existent refund request will return a 404 error. If the refund request has already been approved and processed, the system will return a 400 error to prevent deletion of completed refund processes.

The removal of the refund request record will also remove any audit trail specific to this request. The system will generate a log entry in the audit trail indicating the deletion, including the timestamp and the user ID responsible for the deletion. Related order item states are not affected by this deletion since the refund status is already captured within the order item's own historical status records.

parameters.name: refundRequestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request to be deleted. This UUID corresponds to the refund_request_id field in the shopping_mall_refund_requests database table. The identifier must be valid and exist in the system, or the request will return a 404 error.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: Refund request must be created before it can be deleted. Only after a customer submits a refund request via POST /shoppingMall/customer/refund-requests can it be targeted for deletion.

operations.description:
Compute comprehensive sales performance metrics by aggregating data from the shopping_mall_sales table. This operation provides statistical insights into sales trends and performance without requiring direct access to individual sales records. The metrics include total sales revenue, number of transactions, average transaction value, and sales volume over time.

The operation performs a complex aggregation computation using SQL equivalent to: SELECT SUM(total_amount) as total_revenue, COUNT(*) as transaction_count, AVG(total_amount) as average_transaction_value, SUM(quantity_sold) as total_units_sold FROM shopping_mall_sales WHERE status = 'completed'. This statistical aggregation serves the business need for sales trend analysis without exposing raw sales data.

This operation is designed to meet the requirements for business intelligence reporting specified in the inventory management documentation, allowing management to monitor sales performance, identify trends, and make data-driven decisions about inventory and pricing strategies. It provides a high-level overview of sales metrics that can be used for dashboards and reports.

Important note: This operation does not map directly to any single table in the database as it represents calculated business intelligence data rather than stored entity data. It complements the transactional sales operations by providing analytical insights derived from the same data source.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Perform SQL aggregation on shopping_mall_sales table to compute total revenue, number of transactions, average transaction value, and total units sold. Filter for completed sales only. Use date range parameters if specified in request. Return structured metrics object with computed values. Cache results for 5 minutes to optimize repeated dashboard queries.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive sales performance metrics summarizing total revenue, transaction count, average transaction value, and total units sold.

operations.specification:
Compute aggregate order metrics from shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables.

Query shopping_mall_orders to count total number of orders and sum of total_amount.
Join with shopping_mall_order_items to calculate total revenue (sum of quantity × price) from all order items.
Calculate average order value by dividing total revenue by total order count.
Group orders by status to count number of orders in each status category: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed.

Exclude any orders with status 'deleted' (if exists) or null.

Return all metrics in single response object including:
- orderCount: total number of completed orders
- totalRevenue: sum of all order item amounts (quantity × unit price)
- averageOrderValue: totalRevenue / orderCount
- statusBreakdown: object with count for each status category

Execute as single optimized SQL query with appropriate indexes on created_at and status fields for performance.
operations.description:
Compute aggregated metrics for platform order performance and financial health. This endpoint calculates key business intelligence metrics from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide executives and administrators with an overview of marketplace activity without requiring examination of individual orders.

The operation returns a comprehensive summary including total order volume (orderCount), total revenue generated (totalRevenue), average order value (averageOrderValue), and distribution of orders across all status categories. This aggregated analysis enables strategic decision-making regarding platform growth, fulfillment efficiency, and financial performance. The metrics are calculated from the complete order dataset, using the immutable order and order item snapshots guaranteed by the snapshot principle to ensure auditability and data integrity.

This operation implements a critical analytical requirement for dashboard visibility - it provides an at-a-glance assessment of order patterns without exposing individual customer data. The calculation methodology combines direct order totals from shopping_mall_orders with derived revenue calculations by summing the quantity × price from each associated order item in shopping_mall_order_items. This cross-table aggregation ensures accuracy and prevents data duplication.

The status breakdown provides insight into order fulfillment efficiency by showing how many orders are pending processing, completed, canceled, or refunded. This helps identify potential bottlenecks in the order fulfillment workflow and enables timely intervention if abnormal patterns emerge, such as high cancellation rates in specific seller categories or product types.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive summary of platform order performance metrics.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Compute and return key review analytics metrics for all products on the platform. This operation aggregates data from the shopping_mall_reviews table to calculate overall review metrics that serve business intelligence needs for product owners and administrators.

The operation computes the average rating across all reviews, the total count of reviews, and the distribution of ratings across the 1-5 scale. Since the shopping_mall_reviews table has no delete flags (no status or isDeleted fields), all reviews are included in the analytics calculation regardless of user deletions or administrative actions.

Implementation note: This does NOT map to a single database table - instead it executes:

SELECT
  AVG(rating) as averageRating,
  COUNT(*) as totalCount,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating1Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating2Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating3Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating4Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating5Count
FROM shopping_mall_reviews

This statistical aggregation serves the explicit business need for review analytics as specified in the 13-reviews-and-ratings.md document.

Security considerations: This endpoint requires no authentication as the data is public analytics. The operation will include all reviews from the shopping_mall_reviews table since there are no delete fields in the schema to filter by. The operation has been designed to be read-only and will not affect any review records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_reviews table with JOIN to shopping_mall_review_snapshots.

Calculate average rating, total count, and rating distribution across 1-5 scale.

Use SQL: SELECT AVG(rating) as averageRating, COUNT(*) as totalCount, SUM(CASE WHEN rating = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rating1Count, etc.

Exclude reviews where status = 'deleted_by_admin' (admin-deleted) - these remove rating from average.

Include reviews where isDeleted = true (user-deleted) - these retain rating in average.

Use cached results for 5 minutes with no cache key (global aggregate).

Return JSON object with fields: averageRating, totalCount, rating1Count, rating2Count, rating3Count, rating4Count, rating5Count.

No authentication required - public analytics endpoint.

Return 200 OK with JSON response body.

No transactions or write operations involved.

responseBody.description: Summary statistics for all product reviews on the platform including average rating, total review count, and distribution across the 1-5 rating scale.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated inventory metrics for all product variants across the shopping mall platform.

This operation generates statistical summaries of inventory levels by querying the shopping_mall_inventory_records table, computing key performance indicators for inventory management. It does not return individual inventory records but rather provides high-level insights including total stock count, average stock per variant, and distribution of products by stock status.

The business purpose is to enable sellers and administrators to monitor overall inventory health, identify potential stock issues, and make strategic decisions about restocking and product placement. This aggregated view avoids the performance overhead of retrieving thousands of individual records.

The metrics are calculated by summing the quantityChange field across all inventory records, grouping by variantId, and then aggregating into overall statistics.

Security considerations include restricting access to sellers and administrators, ensuring data privacy for competitor inventories, and implementing rate limiting to prevent API abuse during high-volume reporting periods.

Related operations: GET /inventory/{variantId}/history provides detailed transaction history for a specific variant, while GET /products/{productId}/variants provides current variant inventory status at the product level.

The data returned represents a snapshot of inventory health at the time of request and does not include real-time transactional changes from the shopping cart or checkout system.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Aggregate inventory records from shopping_mall_inventory_records table using GROUP BY variantId. Calculate total stock quantity, average stock per variant, and count of variants with stock below threshold. Filter out records with negative quantities for stock calculation. Return summary statistics including total product variants in stock, total inventory value, and percentage of variants with low stock. Implement pagination for scalable reporting with default page size of 25. Cache results for 15 minutes with variant-based cache key to improve performance. Include query parameters for filtering by inventory status (low_stock, out_of_stock, optimal_stock) and date range.

responseBody.description: Aggregated inventory metrics summary including total product variants, total stock quantity, average stock per variant, and breakdown of inventory status categories.

operations.description:
Approve a seller account that is currently pending administrator review. This operation transitions the seller's status from 'pending_approval' to 'approved', thereby granting the seller full privileges to list products, manage inventory, and receive orders.

This endpoint is exclusively available to administrators or super administrators, as per the Authorization agent's configuration. Upon approval, the system automatically creates an immutable snapshot of the seller's profile as it existed at the time of approval, including shop name, description, and logo URL. This snapshot is preserved in accordance with the snapshot principle documented in 14-snapshot-principle.md.

The initial seller registration process requires email confirmation followed by administrator evaluation. When an administrator approves the seller, the system notifies the seller through email with the message: "Your application has been approved. You may now list products." The approval action is recorded in the audit trail with the administrator ID, IP address, and timestamp.

This operation serves as the final step in the seller onboarding workflow. After approval, the seller gains access to the seller dashboard and can begin submitting product listings. Existing rejection reasons are cleared, and the seller can reapply if previously rejected. Previous refusal history is retained for compliance but does not interfere with approval.

This endpoint does not modify the seller's profile directly — it only changes the approval status and triggers the snapshot creation. Profile updates must be handled through PUT /sellers/me. Prior to approval, the seller account is inactive and cannot engage in commerce on the platform.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sellers table with sellerId matching path parameter. Verify seller status is 'pending_approval'. Set status to 'approved', clear any rejection_reason and deleted_at if present. Create an immutable seller profile snapshot with current profile data (shopName, shopDescription, logoImageUrl), action: 'approve', actorId (from auth context), and timestamp. Send notification email to seller. Log approval event in audit table with sellerId, adminId, IP, and action.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller account to be approved.
parameters.name: sellerId

responseBody.description: Confirmation that the seller account has been successfully approved.

operations.description:
Reject a seller's registration application.

This operation permanently denies a seller's application to join the platform as a selling entity. It is performed by an administrator after reviewing the seller's registration details. Once a seller is rejected, they cannot proceed with selling on the platform until a new registration is submitted. This action triggers a system snapshot of the rejection decision for audit and compliance purposes.

The rejection must include a reason (minimum 10 characters) that explains why the application was denied, and this reason will be provided to the seller via email. Rejected seller accounts cannot log in, cannot create products, and have their shop name hidden from all public listings. If a rejected seller later submits a new application, the system will reset their status to "pending_approval" but will preserve all historical rejection records and snapshots.

This operation follows the business logic defined in the 03-seller-account.md requirements document, which states: "WHEN an administrator rejects a seller, THE system SHALL set status to 'rejected', require administrator to enter a rejection reason (minimum 10 characters), and notify seller via email." Here, the reason is provided in the request body by the administrator.

If the seller id does not exist, the system returns 404 Not Found. If the seller has already been approved or is suspended, the system returns 400 Bad Request rejecting the request because only pending applications can be rejected. The seller profile snapshot is created automatically by the system at the time of this rejection.

Related operations: PATCH /sellers/{sellerId}/approve (to approve a seller), POST /sellers/{sellerId}/reapply (for rejected sellers to reapply).
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Update shopping_mall_sellers set status = 'rejected', rejection_reason = $reason, updated_at = now() where seller_id = $sellerId and status = 'pending_approval'.
Check if seller_id exists and status is 'pending_approval', otherwise return 404 or 400 respectively.
Create a snapshot of shopping_mall_sellers state with rejection reason and timestamp, linking it to the operation.
Log this rejection event with administrator ID and IP address for audit trail.
Send email to seller with rejection reason if email address is verified.
Return 204 No Content on success.
Use database transaction for atomic update and snapshot creation.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller whose registration is being rejected. Must exist in the shopping_mall_sellers table and have status 'pending_approval'.
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: The reason for rejecting the seller's registration. Must be at least 10 characters long and explain the decision clearly for compliance purposes.

operations.specification: Find seller by id in shopping_mall_sellers table. If seller does not exist, return 404. If seller already suspended, return 409 Conflict. Set seller is_suspended to true, update suspended_at timestamp, and log suspension event in shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots. Do not change account status or delete records—suspension is a temporary restriction. Trigger system-wide access restrictions: hide shop from catalog, disable product publishing, nullify pending orders, revoke authentication tokens.
operations.description:
Admin-only endpoint to permanently suspend a seller account.

This operation immediately restricts all actions by a suspended seller across the entire shopping mall platform. When a seller is suspended, their shop becomes fully invisible to customers—their products disappear from search results, storefronts, and category listings. All authentication tokens for this seller are immediately revoked, preventing any future access to seller-facing interfaces. The seller's account is preserved with all associated data, but any new orders or promotions they attempt to create are automatically rejected. Existing order fulfillment may be suspended pending review, with notifications sent to affected buyers.

Suspension is a restricted administrative action that must be performed by admin or superAdmin roles with appropriate authority. The suspension action does not delete the seller account or erase any historical data, preserving audit trails and compliance records. Suspended sellers can be reinstated later by an administrator if applicable and appropriate. The system will create an immutable profile snapshot capturing the exact state of the seller's shop before suspension, including shop name, description, and profile image.

This operation is deliberately not idempotent and uses the POST method because suspension is considered an actionable event, not a state update. A separate endpoint exists for unsuspension. The suspension must only occur if the target seller exists and is not already suspended.

parameters.name: sellerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target seller account to suspend. This must match the seller's primary key 'id' in the shopping_mall_sellers table. This UUID is system-generated upon seller registration and remains unchanged throughout the seller's lifecycle.

operations.name: suspend

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sellers table with sellerId parameter. Verify seller status is 'suspended' before updating to 'active'. Update status and clear suspension_reason if exists. Log action in audit trail. Return updated seller record. Enforce admin authorization before execution.
operations.description:
Reinstate a suspended seller account to active status in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows administrators to restore seller account privileges after suspension due to policy violations, compliance reviews, or temporary administrative holds. The seller must currently have a status of 'suspended' for this operation to succeed; attempting to reinstate already active or pending sellers will result in an error.

The system automatically clears the suspension reason field upon successful reinstatement and updates the updated_at timestamp. A complete audit log entry is created recording who performed the reinstatement and when. All associated seller data including shop name, products, and customer relationships remain unchanged and instantly become accessible to customers again. The seller receives a system notification of the status change.

This operation is restricted to administrators with seller management permissions. It does not modify any other aspects of the seller's profile, pending orders, or financial status. The operation performs a direct status transition from 'suspended' to 'active' according to the shopping_mall_sellers database schema which does not support soft delete functionality.

parameters.name: sellerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller account to be reinstated. This UUID corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_sellers table.

responseBody.description: The updated seller account information after successful reinstatement.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Seller must be in suspended state before reinstatement can be performed. The suspend operation creates the necessary state dependency for this reinstatement operation.

operations.description:
Permanently ban a customer account from the shopping mall platform.

This operation suspends all access for the specified customer, preventing any further login, browsing, purchases, or interactions with the platform. It is an administrative action that must be executed by users with admin or super admin privileges. The ban is permanent and irreversible from the customer perspective.

The ban is implemented by setting the isBanned field to true and isActive field to false in the shopping_mall_customers table. The customer's account remains in the database to preserve order history, reviews, and audit trails, but is completely inaccessible. The customer cannot register again with the same email address, and all associated data (cart, wishlist, reviews) remains intact for compliance and historical purposes.

Security: Only authenticated admins or super admins can invoke this endpoint. Authorization is handled by the Endpoint agent based on user role. This operation does not delete any data, ensuring compliance with data retention policies for order history and legal requirements.

Related operations: POST /admin/customers/{customerId}/unban to restore access for a banned customer, GET /customers/manage to list all banned customers for administrative review.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Update the shopping_mall_customers table to set isBanned = true and isActive = false for the specified customerId. Log the action in an audit trail table with admin identity and timestamp. Ensure the operation only proceeds if the requesting user has admin or super admin role. Validate that customerId is a valid UUID format before database update. Return 204 No Content on success. If customer is already banned, return 409 Conflict. If customerId does not exist, return 404 Not Found. No transactions or complex logic involved - single database update.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer to be banned. Must be a valid UUID format and must correspond to an existing customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table.
parameters.name: customerId

prerequisites.description: A customer must verify their email address to create a valid account before they can be banned.

operations.description:
Administratively restore access to a previously banned customer account. This operation updates the customer's status from 'banned' to 'active' in the shopping_mall_customers table, allowing the customer to log in and use the platform again. This action can only be performed by administrators and is typically used when a customer has fulfilled remediation requirements or when a ban was issued in error.

Administrators may use this operation to reverse bans based on policy review or customer appeal. The system logs this action in the administration audit trail and preserves the original ban record for compliance and dispute resolution. When a customer is unbanned, all previous order history, reviews, wishlist items, and address data remain intact and are immediately accessible.

Security: This operation is restricted to administrators with proper authentication. The system verifies the requester's administrative role and logs the administrator ID and timestamp of the unban action. Multiple unban attempts on the same customer are permitted if revoked and re-applied.

This operation does not affect the customer's financial history, reviews, products in wishlist, or any associated order records. Customer information including email and display name remain unchanged; only the status field is modified.

Related operations: Admins may use PATCH /admin/customers/{customerId}/ban to re-ban a customer who violates policy again after unban.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update the banned status of customer in shopping_mall_customers table from true to false based on customerId path parameter. Validate that requester has admin role. Log administrative action in audit table with timestamp, administrator ID, and target customer ID. Return 200 OK on success. Return 403 Forbidden if requester is not an admin. Return 404 Not Found if customer ID does not exist. Do not modify any other customer fields or related data.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer account to unban
parameters.name: customerId

prerequisites.description: Customer email verification record must be created to confirm customer account exists before unban can be performed.

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for an order item that has status 'paid'. This operation initiates the cancellation workflow for an order item but does not immediately cancel the item.

This operation allows customers to request cancellation of order items before shipment. The cancellation request must include a reason (minimum 10 characters) explaining why the item should be cancelled. The request is then queued for review by the seller, who may approve or reject the cancellation within 48 hours.

Security: Only authenticated customers can submit cancellation requests. The system verifies the requesting user owns the order item. The operation checks that the order item status is 'paid' before allowing submission. If the item status is 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded', the request will fail with a 400 error.

This operation triggers the creation of a cancellation request snapshot as defined in the Snapshot Principle. The snapshot captures the request reason, timestamp, customer ID, order item ID, and initial status ('pending'). The snapshot is immutable and preserved for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Relationship to other operations: This operation is followed by PUT /orders/{orderId}/items/{orderItemId}/cancel-response, which allows the seller to approve or reject the cancellation request. Upon approval, the order item status changes to 'cancelled' and inventory is restored by a positive inventory record with reason 'cancellation'. Upon rejection, the status remains 'paid'. If no response is received within 48 hours, the system automatically approves the cancellation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a new cancellation request record in the database with status 'pending'. Validate that the order item exists and has status 'paid'. Validate that the request reason is at least 10 characters. Create a cancellation request snapshot with the reason, timestamp, customer ID, and order item ID. Return the created cancellation request record with its unique ID and status. Send notification to the seller of the product. Do not modify the order item status. Handle concurrent requests appropriately to ensure idempotency.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target order. This is a globally unique UUID generated at order creation.
parameters.name: orderId

operations.description:
Initiate a refund request for a specific order item after delivery has been confirmed. This operation allows the customer to formally request a refund for a product they have received, providing a reason for the refund. The refund request is stored in the system with a 'pending' status, requiring approval from the seller before any financial transaction occurs. This mechanism ensures proper audit trails and prevents unauthorized refund requests.

The refund request is linked to the specific order item through the orderItem_id field, ensuring each refund request relates to exactly one product in one order. The reason field explicitly captures the customer’s justification, which can be used by sellers during approval evaluation and by administrators during dispute resolution. The creation of a refund request automatically triggers email notifications to both the seller and the absent customer.

This operation does not immediately process the refund or update inventory or payment status. Those actions occur only after seller approval via the PUT /orders/{orderId}/items/{orderItemId}/refund-response endpoint. The refund request record is immutable once created, preserving the original customer statement for audit purposes. Subsequent changes are recorded in snapshots as described in the 14-snapshot-principle.md document.

Following customer refund requests, sellers may approve or reject the request. Approved requests trigger automatic refund processing via the payment provider, with funds returned to the original payment method. Goods returned by the customer (if applicable) are handled separately through the return shipping workflow. Rejected requests remain in the system with the seller's rejection reason documented.

Related operations: 
- PUT /orders/{orderId}/items/{orderItemId}/refund-response - Seller response to refund request
- GET /orders/{orderId}/items - Retrieve full order details including refund request statuses
- POST /orders/{orderId}/items/{orderItemId}/cancel - Similar workflow for order item cancellation
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Insert a new refund_request with order_item_id, customer_id, reason, and status 'pending'. Link to order and order item via foreign keys. Use current timestamp for created_at. Send notification to seller and customer. Return 201 Created with full refund request details. Validate that order_item exists and is in 'delivered' status before allowing refund request. Reject if status is not 'delivered'.

parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific order item within the order for which the refund is being requested.
parameters.name: orderItemId

responseBody.description: Details of the created refund request record.

Order must be created from cart before order items exist and can be refunded

operations.description:
Permanently delete a review report that was filed against a specific review.

This operation removes a report record from the shopping_mall_review_reports table, which documents a complaint or abuse filed by a user regarding a specific review. Reports are created when users identify reviews as spam, harassment, or other violations, but they are not visible to end-users; they serve an internal moderation purpose.

This operation is irreversible and permanently purges the report record from the system, removing all tracking information about the report including its reason, reporter ID, and timestamp. The underlying review is unaffected and remains visible to all users unless individual review deletion is performed.

Security: The user making this request must be an administrator or super administrator. Regular users cannot delete review reports. Access is determined by the Endpoint agent based on authentication and role verification. Only system moderators have the authority to purge reports for system integrity.

This operation preserves the integrity of the audit trail: reports are not soft-deleted but permanently removed from the database, allowing systems to maintain accurate moderation statistics without cluttering records with expired or resolved reports. No snapshot is created for this operation because it pertains to metadata cleanup rather than content modification.

Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId}/reports (list all reports), POST /reviews/{reviewId}/reports (create a new report).
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_reports table using review_id and report_id as composite foreign keys.
Perform a hard delete (not soft delete) of the record. Log this action to system audit trail with actor, timestamp, and entity UID. Return 204 No Content on success. Validate actor has admin or super_admin role before deletion.

operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator request to become a regular administrator. This operation transitions an administrator request from pending state to approved state, granting the requested user administrator privileges on the shopping mall platform. The operation is only accessible to super administrators with elevated privileges.

The system tracks all administrator requests in the shopping_mall_admins table. When a user submits an admin request through the POST /admins/requests endpoint, a record is created with status 'pending'. This endpoint accepts a specific adminRequestId as a path parameter to uniquely identify which request to approve. Upon successful approval, the shopping_mall_admins record is updated to set the approval status to 'approved' and the associated user account is granted administrator role permissions.

This operation is a critical part of the platform's role management system. It ensures that only super administrators can grant administrative privileges, maintaining proper access control hierarchy. The approval process is logged but does not require additional input beyond the adminRequestId, as the approval intent is inherent in the endpoint design. Related operations include POST /admins/requests (submit request), DELETE /admins/requests/{adminRequestId} (reject request), and PATCH /admins/{adminId}/upgrade (promote existing admin to super admin).

Security: This endpoint requires authentication with valid JWT and super admin privileges. Unauthorized access attempts will be denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden. The adminRequestId must be a valid UUID for an existing pending admin request, otherwise HTTP 404 Not Found will be returned.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admins table for record with matching adminRequestId status == 'pending'. If record found and status is 'pending', update record to set status: 'approved' and set approvedAt: current timestamp. Return 204 No Content response. If record not found or status not 'pending', return 404 Not Found. Only super admin users (admin_type == 'super') are authorized. Verify JWT token and user privileges before processing. Log approval event for audit trail.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the admin request to approve. Must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing pending admin request record in the shopping_mall_admins table.
parameters.name: adminRequestId

prerequisites.description: A pending administrator request must be created first using this operation to generate the adminRequestId that the approve operation requires.

operations.description:
Reject an administrator request submitted by a user. This operation allows a super administrator to formally deny a request to become an administrator.

The rejection is permanent and non-reversible. When a request is rejected, the requesting user is notified via system notification and cannot reapply for a minimum of 30 days, as specified in the business requirements. The rejection must include a reason that documents the specific justification for denial, which is recorded in the audit trail.

The system MUST create a snapshot of the rejection decision, capturing the state of the request before rejection, the rejection reason provided, the timestamp, and the identity of the rejecting super administrator. This snapshot is immutable and serves as official record for compliance and dispute resolution.

Note that this operation is specifically designed for the admin request workflow in the administrator promotion process, not for regular user account actions. It operates on the admin request entity, not on the user account directly. The rejection does not delete the request record - it updates its status to 'rejected' while preserving all historical data.

Administrators who are not super administrators cannot perform this action. The system will validate that the calling user has super administrator privileges before executing the operation.

Related operations: POST /admins/requests to submit an admin request, POST /admins/requests/{adminRequestId}/approve to approve an admin request.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Update the admin request status to 'rejected' in the database. Create a snapshot of the admin request record including: request ID, user ID, requested role, reason, creation timestamp, status, and rejection reason. Record the super administrator ID and timestamp of rejection. Apply transaction to ensure both status update and snapshot creation are atomic. Send system notification to the requesting user with rejection reason. Return 200 Success on completion or 403 Forbidden if caller lacks super admin privileges.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the admin request to reject.
parameters.name: adminRequestId

requestBody.description: The reason for rejecting the administrator role request.

responseBody.description: Confirmation that the admin request has been successfully rejected.

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator status.

This operation is exclusively accessible to super administrators and is used to elevate a regular admin to full system-level privileges. Only admins with adminType 'regular' can be promoted. This change grants the promoted admin full permissions over all other administrators, including promotion, demotion, and oversight of the entire platform.

The operation does not require a request body because the action is implied by the endpoint path. The admin to be promoted is identified by the adminId in the path parameter. Upon successful execution, the adminType field in the shopping_mall_admins database table is updated from 'regular' to 'super'.

All admin promotion requests must be audited in the system's audit log, capturing the identity of the approving super admin and the timestamp of the change.

This operation cannot be reversed by regular admins or other super admins. Only system-level recovery procedures can downgrade a super admin.

Related operations: PATCH /admins/{adminId}/downgrade
operations.name: upgrade
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admins table for the admin with provided adminId. Validate that the current adminType is 'regular' and that the calling user has adminType 'super'. If valid, update the adminType to 'super' using a database transaction. Log the promotion event in the audit trail. Return updated admin object with new adminType. Throw 403 if caller is not a super admin or target is not a regular admin. Throw 404 if adminId does not exist.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator to promote. Must be a valid UUID reference in the shopping_mall_admins table.
parameters.name: adminId

responseBody.description: Response body containing confirmation of upgrade and updated admin type.

operations.specification: Perform an admin downgrade operation by updating the adminType field in the shopping_mall_admins table from 'regular' to 'user'. Authenticate request with super-admin JWT token. Verify target adminId exists and has adminType 'regular'. Log administrative downgrade action in system audit logs. Return 204 No Content on success. Return 403 Forbidden if requester is not a super-admin. Return 404 Not Found if adminId does not exist or is not a regular admin. Return 409 Conflict if target is already a super-admin or non-admin.
operations.description:
Demote a regular administrator to standard user status with all administrative privileges removed.

This privileged operation allows super-administrators to demote regular administrators by changing their adminType from 'regular' to 'user'. The targeted admin loses all administrative capabilities and reverts to standard user status with only member-level permissions. This action cannot be undone and automatically triggers system audit logging for compliance tracking.

Authorization: Only super-administrators may invoke this endpoint. The system validates the requesting user's admin_type field in their JWT token to ensure they have the required super-admin privileges. No one can downgrade themselves or other super-administrators.

Security: This action is irreversible and permanently removes administrative access. The target admin's authentication token remains active until expiration but loses all administrative permissions upon next validation. Any pending administrative tasks associated with the downgraded user are flagged for reassignment.

Related operations: /admins/{adminId}/upgrade (promote user to admin), /admins/requests (approve admin applications), /admins/manage (list all admins).

parameters.name: adminId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the regular administrator to be downgraded (scoped to regular admin accounts)

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products matching search criteria with advanced filtering and sorting. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_products table and supports multi-dimensional search across product name, category, price range, and stock availability. Search term performs case-insensitive partial match on product name across all products regardless of seller status or deletion flag.

Security considerations require authenticted customer access only. Unauthenticated users are not permitted to access the search endpoint. Search results respect product visibility rules: only show active products with at least one active variant and from approved (not suspended) sellers.

When filtering by category, the system includes products in the selected category and all associated subcategories. Price range filtering uses the minimum variant price for products with multiple variants, or base price for products with single variants. The inStockOnly filter excludes products where all variants have zero or negative stock, ensuring only available products are returned. Sorting supports three modes: newest first (by creation timestamp), price low to high (by minimum variant price), and price high to low (by maximum variant price). Results are returned with pagination parameters including total count and current page information.

This operation integrates with the Product Service to ensure real-time accuracy of product data, including current inventory levels and seller status. It does not return product details or variants directly but provides summarized information for display in listings. Product details can be retrieved individually via GET /products/{productId} endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_products table with left joins to product variants, seller profiles, and product categories. Apply filters based on search term (ILIKE on name), category hierarchy (using category_id tree), price range (min/max variant price), and stock availability (sum of inventory records > 0). Sort results based on requested criteria: createdAt DESC for newest, min_variant_price ASC for price low to high, max_variant_price DESC for price high to low. Implement cursor-based pagination using createdAt and productId for infinite scroll support. Build response with only essential summary fields: productId, name, basePrice, categoryName, sellerName, imageUrl, averageRating, reviewCount, isAvailable, variantCount. Cache results for 5 minutes with cache key including search parameters to improve performance under load. Convert product summaries to IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary type structure for response.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for product filtering including search term, category, price range, in-stock only flag, and sorting preference.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summary information matching search criteria with total count and pagination metadata.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all products across the entire shopping mall platform for administrative oversight and compliance. This operation returns comprehensive product information including product names, seller associations, category associations, and each product's creation and update timestamps to enable platform administrators to perform complete inventory auditing and policy enforcement.

The endpoint provides access to all active products within the system regardless of seller, status, or category, allowing administrators to monitor product activity across the entire ecosystem. This functionality is essential for platform governance, enabling admins to identify potentially problematic listings (such as duplicated products, banned seller inventory, or products violating content policies), verify compliance with marketplace rules, and manage product lifecycle across all sellers.

Administrators can use this endpoint to generate comprehensive reports on product volume, track product creation patterns among sellers, identify inactive or abandoned product listings, and audit product categorization consistency. This is a critical tool for platform security and quality control, ensuring consistent implementation of platform policies across a potentially large number of sellers.

When a product has been flagged for violation or policy breach, administrators use this list to locate the product and take appropriate action such as deletion, suspension, or notification.

Note: Products that have been deleted are permanently removed from the database and are not included in this list. This operation returns only products that still exist in the system.

The response includes all key product information: productId for unique identification, name for product identification, sellerId for seller association, categoryId for category classification, and creation/update timestamps. Each product's creation and update timestamps are included to facilitate analysis of product lifecycle patterns. The operation does not include product variants, images, pricing, or inventory - those details are available via dedicated endpoints but are excluded here to maintain focus on administrative overview and compliance purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_products table with pagination using page and limit query parameters. Order results by createdAt descending to show most recent products first. Include only productId, name, sellerId, categoryId, isDeleted, createdAt, and updatedAt fields from the product table as specified in the schema. Join with shopping_mall_sellers table to retrieve sellerName for display purposes. Apply authorization check to ensure only admin or superAdmin roles can access this endpoint. Use cursor-based pagination if dataset exceeds 10,000 items for performance optimization. Cache results for 5 minutes with cache key generated from query parameters. Return 403 Forbidden if requester lacks admin privileges.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of all products with administrative metadata for auditing and compliance purposes. Each object contains essential product information including primary identifier, name, seller association, category classification, and timestamps to enable comprehensive administrative oversight and platform governance.

operations.description:
Compute monthly sales statistics by aggregating data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables using GROUP BY month.

This operation provides a comprehensive view of sales performance over time. It calculates total revenue, total order count, average order value, and other key metrics for each month, enabling users to identify sales trends and seasonal patterns.

Implementation note: This does NOT map to a single database table - instead it executes:

SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('month', o.created_at) as month,
  COUNT(*) as order_count,
  SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) as revenue,
  AVG(oi.quantity * oi.price) as average_order_value,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as delivered_order_count
FROM shopping_mall_orders o
JOIN shopping_mall_order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'shipped', 'delivered')
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.created_at)
ORDER BY month DESC

This statistical aggregation serves the business need for sales trend analysis and informs inventory planning, marketing campaigns, and financial forecasting.

Security considerations: Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated users with appropriate permissions (typically admin or dashboard users). Rate limiting is applied to prevent API abuse.

Related operations: This data can be visualized in conjunction with GET /products/search for product-level sales analysis and GET /sellers/me/dashboard for seller-specific performance tracking.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables using GROUP BY month to compute sales statistics. Join orders with order items to calculate revenue from quantities and prices. Filter for orders with status 'paid', 'shipped', or 'delivered'. Aggregate results to compute: order count, total revenue, average order value, and delivered order count. Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Cache results for 15 minutes with cache key based on query parameters and user permissions. Apply rate limiting of 100 requests per minute per user. Return results sorted by month in descending order (newest first).

responseBody.description: Paginated statistical data showing monthly sales performance including total revenue, order count, average order value, and delivered order count for each month.

operations.description:
Compute and return statistical analytics on the effectiveness of product promotions across the shoppingMall platform. This operation aggregates data from Sales, OrderItems, and Promotions to calculate key marketing performance indicators.

The endpoint returns metrics including total sales revenue generated by each promotion, average discount rate applied, number of unique customers who used the promotion, conversion rate (sales generated vs total views), and total units sold. This enables marketing teams to evaluate the ROI of promotional campaigns and make data-driven decisions for future promotions.

The analytics engine joins the ShoppingMallSales table with ShoppingMallSalePromotions and ShoppingMallOrderItems tables to track promotion usage and revenue impact. Each promotion's effectiveness is calculated by comparing the total revenue generated during the promotion period against a baseline period, and the conversion rate is calculated as the number of sales made with the promotion divided by the total number of product views.

Security considerations: This endpoint is accessible only to administrators and marketing staff with appropriate permissions. Regular customers and sellers cannot access promotional analytics data.

Related operations: This endpoint should be used in conjunction with PATCH /products to analyze the effect of promotion changes on specific products. Performance metrics from this endpoint should inform the creation and modification of product-level promotions.

Error handling: If no promotions exist over the requested time period, an empty result set will be returned without error. If invalid time parameters are provided (e.g., end date before start date), a 400 error will be returned with a descriptive message about the invalid parameters.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Join ShoppingMallSales with ShoppingMallSalePromotions and ShoppingMallOrderItems tables to calculate promotion effectiveness metrics. Aggregate sales data by promotionId, calculating total revenue, average discount percentage, unique customer count, and units sold. Apply date range filtering based on query parameters (start_date and end_date). Group results by promotionId and sort by revenue generated in descending order. Implement pagination with cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Cache results for 15 minutes using promotionId and date range as cache keys. Return metrics: revenue, discountRate, uniqueCustomers, unitsSold, conversionRate, promotionName, promotionType. Include empty results if no promotions match criteria, no 404 error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of promotion effectiveness analytics with aggregated metrics for each promotion.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated performance metrics for the authenticated seller's shop on the shoppingMall platform.

This performance dashboard operation calculates key business indicators based on historical order and sales data captured via the platform's snapshot principle. All metrics are computed from immutable order snapshots that preserve the exact state of products, variants, seller profiles, and pricing at the moment of purchase, ensuring historical accuracy. The calculation excludes any products or variants that have been deleted by the seller after the order was placed, as these are not reflected in the order snapshots.

Performance metrics are updated in real-time as new orders are completed, and all data is sourced directly from the system's finalized order records and product snapshots. Notably, due to the snapshot principle, a seller's current product price changes or inventory levels do not affect the historical performance data — the metrics reflect the actual transaction conditions at the time of sale.

The revenue figure includes only completed payments and excludes refunds or cancellations. The average order value and number of customers represent unique customers who completed any purchase from the seller's shop. Customer retention is calculated based on repeat purchase behavior, defined as customers making more than one purchase.

This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated sellers and is never available to customers or administrators, preserving data privacy and adhering to role-based access controls as defined in the platform specifications.

Related operations: GET /products — for individual product performance; GET /orders — for detailed order inspection; GET /inventory — for current stock levels.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sale_view_stats to extract total sales and revenue for the authenticated seller's account. Join with shopping_mall_orders to count total orders and unique customer IDs. Join with shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_sellers to ensure only active (non-deleted) products are included. Compute average order value by dividing total revenue by total orders. Calculate customer retention rate as: (customers with multiple orders / total customers) * 100. Sum all order item quantities to determine total units sold. Aggregate all metrics in a single query with grouping. Cache results for 5 minutes using seller ID as cache key. Return a single aggregated record with all performance fields. Apply pagination only if extended reports are requested in future.

responseBody.description: Contains aggregated performance summary metrics for the seller's shop on the shoppingMall platform.

operations.description:
This endpoint computes product engagement metrics by aggregating customer behavior data across the shoppingMall platform. The data is derived from the shopping_mall_sales, shopping_mall_cart_items, and shopping_mall_review_snapshots tables. Each product's engagement score represents its popularity and customer interaction strength, enabling strategic insights into product performance.

The operation calculates the following metrics per product: total sales count, total cart additions, average review rating, total review count, and total revenue generated. These are grouped by product_id and product_name, returning a comprehensive view of which products drive the most customer activity and revenue. Data includes only active products with approved sellers and excludes deleted or suspended products.

Security and authorization: This endpoint is restricted to administrators and super administrators due to the sensitivity of strategic business insights. Regular customers and sellers do not have access to this level of analytics. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this resource-heavy query. The metrics are computed in real-time without caching to ensure data accuracy during reporting cycles.

Comparison with other endpoints: Unlike GET /products which returns product listings and variants, this endpoint does not return variant-level or individual transaction data. It is a higher-level aggregate view that complements product management features by providing data-driven insights. External tools such as reporting dashboards rely on this endpoint to visualize product performance trends over time. The metrics are also used internally to power recommendation engines and inventory forecasting models.

Database dependencies: This operation relies on the integrity of the shopping_mall_sales table for completed transactions, shopping_mall_cart_items for pre-purchase interest, and shopping_mall_review_snapshots for customer feedback. All product and seller status fields are filtered to ensure only active and approved entities contribute to the result.

Performance optimization: The system utilizes indexed views on the underlying tables to optimize aggregation performance. Aggregation joins are optimized and computed with efficient GROUP BY clauses. The response includes pagination to handle large datasets efficiently without performance degradation.

Error handling: If no sales or cart data exists for products, metrics default to zero. The operation avoids complex nested joins and maintains a flat structure for reliability. The specification ensures clarity for downstream agents implementing the service layer logic.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_sales table to count total sales per product, sum revenue, and join with shopping_mall_cart_items to count cart additions. Join with shopping_mall_review_snapshots to calculate average rating and total reviews. Group by product_id and product_name. Filter for active products (isDeleted = false) and active sellers (approvalStatus = 'approved'). For each group, compute: sales_count = COUNT(sales.id), cart_additions = COUNT(cart_items.id), avg_rating = AVG(reviews.rating), review_count = COUNT(reviews.id), total_revenue = SUM(sales.total_amount). Use pagination with limit and offset. Do not cache results; computations are done on-the-fly for accuracy. Log query execution time for performance monitoring.

responseBody.description: Paginated response containing aggregated product engagement metrics for business analytics.

operations.name: meMetrics

Query the shopping_mall_cart_items table to calculate cart statistics.
- Calculate total quantity of all cart items: SUM(quantity)
- Calculate count of unique cart items: COUNT(DISTINCT variantId)
- Calculate total cart value: SUM(quantity * unit_price)
- Calculate number of available items: COUNT where isAvailable = true and stockQuantity > 0
- Calculate number of unavailable items: COUNT where isAvailable = false or stockQuantity = 0

This information enables sellers and administrators to detect inventory trends, identify anomalies, and optimize restocking strategies.

The service layer implements UTC-based time window grouping to generate daily, weekly, or monthly summaries based on query parameters. The query joins with shopping_mall_product_variants to include variant details while preserving performance through indexing on variant_id and created_at.

Aggregate system-wide review statistics across all products.

This operation computes the overall average rating and total count of reviews for the entire shopping mall platform. The average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews in the shopping_mall_reviews table, with user-deleted reviews still contributing their rating value to the average (as specified in review system requirements), while admin-deleted reviews are excluded from both rating calculation and count.

This endpoint serves as a high-level system metric for platform health and user satisfaction monitoring. The average rating is dynamically calculated and rounded to one decimal place on every request to ensure real-time accuracy, reflecting the current state of the review system as modified by all user and admin actions. The total review count represents the number of non-deleted reviews currently visible on the platform.

This operation supports no filters or parameters because it provides a system-wide summary rather than product-specific metrics. It complements the product-specific review endpoints by providing a top-level overview of review sentiment across the entire platform.

The result is used in admin dashboards, platform analytics reports, and public-facing statistics displays. This operation must not be used to update or modify any review data - it is strictly a read-only aggregation endpoint.

Return the result as an object with averageRating and totalCount properties. Cache the result for 30 seconds to improve performance for frequent requests. The cache key should be based on the exact query parameters (no parameters here, so use static cache key). Use read-only database connection for this aggregation to avoid transaction overhead. Do not include any user-specific data or personal information in the response. Return 200 OK with the statistics object.

Permanently remove a category from the platform's category hierarchy.

This administrative operation performs a hard delete of the specified category, removing it from the shopping_mall_sections table. This is a destructive action that permanently eliminates the category and all of its associated metadata from the system. When this operation is executed, the category record is completely removed from the database, with no possibility of recovery.

The operation validates that the category can be safely deleted before proceeding. Specifically, it checks that no products are using this category as their primary category, and that the category has no child categories that would become orphaned by this deletion. This validation is critical as product categorization is a key business function and orphaned categories would create data integrity issues.

This operation is strictly restricted to administrators with appropriate authorization. Regular users cannot delete categories as this would compromise the structural integrity of the product taxonomy. Upon successful deletion, the system logs the action for audit purposes, but does not create a snapshot of the deleted category as hard deletion by definition does not preserve historical data.

Return 204 No Content on success.

This API does not directly interact with a persistent database table; instead, category metadata is managed through the system's configuration storage, ensuring fast access and consistency across distributed services. The category data is immutable in the sense that it cannot be deleted once created (though it may be archived or superseded), aligning with the platform's snapshot principle for auditability.
